mn12:3.3: “The ascetic Gotama has no superhuman distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones.

mn12:3.5: Regardless of his goal in teaching the Dhamma, it delivers one who applies it to the complete ending of suffering.”

mn12:36.4: And I understand how someone practicing that way, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the animal realm.

mn12:36.8: And I understand how someone practicing that way, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn among human beings.
mn12:37.9: In the same way, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand:
mn12:37.10: ‘This individual is practicing in such a way and is riding upon such a path that when their body breaks up, after death, they will be reborn in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.’
mn12:37.11: Some time later I see that they have indeed been reborn in hell, where they experience absolutely painful feelings, sharp and severe.
mn12:38.9: In the same way, when I’ve comprehended the mind of an individual, I understand:
mn12:38.10: ‘This individual is practicing in such a way and is riding upon such a path that when their body breaks up, after death, they will be reborn in the animal realm.’
mn12:38.11: Some time later I see that they have indeed been reborn in the animal realm, where they suffer painful feelings, sharp and severe.

mn12:48.9: So that I wouldn’t see them, nor they me.
mn12:53-55.7: So they eat ordinary rice and rice powder, and drink rice water.
mn12:53-55.8: And they enjoy many rice concoctions.
mn12:53-55.9: I recall eating just a single grain of rice.
mn12:53-55.11: at that time the grains of rice must have been very big.
mn12:53-55.12: But you should not see it like this.
mn12:53-55.13: The grains of rice then were at most the same size as today.
mn12:53-55.14: Eating so very little, my body became severely emaciated.
mn12:53-55.15: Due to eating so little, my major and minor limbs became like the joints of an eighty-year-old or a dying man,
mn12:53-55.16: my bottom became like a camel’s hoof,
mn12:53-55.17: my vertebrae stuck out like beads on a string,
mn12:53-55.18: and my ribs were as gaunt as the broken-down rafters on an old barn.
mn12:53-55.19: Due to eating so little, the gleam of my eyes sank deep in their sockets, like the gleam of water sunk deep down a well.
mn12:53-55.20: Due to eating so little, my scalp shriveled and withered like a green bitter-gourd in the wind and sun.
mn12:53-55.21: Due to eating so little, the skin of my belly stuck to my backbone, so that when I tried to rub the skin of my belly I grabbed my backbone, and when I tried to rub my backbone I rubbed the skin of my belly.
mn12:53-55.22: Due to eating so little, when I tried to urinate or defecate I fell face down right there.
